name: media_rss_sweep
what: Live RSS sweep of 8 popular Indian newspapers' section feeds -- Economic Times, Hindu, Hindu Business Line, Times of India, Livemint, Moneycontrol, Business Standard (English) + Amar Ujala (Hindi) -- filtered for investment-intent language (English + Devanagari keywords), matched against real 23-country foreign stock-market rosters (same files layer 42 uses). Full article text pulled only for roster-confirmed hits. Originally a workaround for ET/Hindu/HBL blocking Anthropic's hosted crawler/search infra outright -- runs via subprocess curl from the local machine, which is never blocked (see feedback_economic_times_blocked memory) -- kept as the standard fetch method when extended to more sources for consistency. CAVEAT on the Hindi source: company-name matching only catches names Indian financial press conventionally leaves in Latin script (Apple, Tesla, Toyota); transliterated names (e.g. एप्पल for Apple) are invisible to the shared Latin-script matcher -- partial, not full, non-English coverage. Separate CAVEAT: 'strong' fragment matches on generic industry-descriptive company names (e.g. 'Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corp' vs. any article about semiconductor manufacturing in general) still slip through even after the SPAC/share-class filter -- treat every match here as a candidate for human review via its full_text field, not a confirmed lead, same as layer 44's un-reviewed MoU rows.

matches.company: CNH Industrial N.V. Common Shares
matches.title: CM Yogi Adityanath promotes UP's 'bulldozer brand', invites CNH to manufacture them alongside tractors
matches.full_text: Lucknow: Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Thursday described bulldozers as a brand associated with the state and suggested that CNH Industrial, which is setting up a tractor manufacturing plant in Gautam Buddh Nagar, could also manufacture them in Uttar Pradesh.The bulldozer has emerged as a potent political symbol of the Adityanath-led government in UP, representing its  tough-on-crime  and  anti-encroachment  image, while also becoming a rallying point for supporters and a subject of opposition criticism over alleged selective demolitions. You must have heard about Uttar Pradesh's bulldozer. I would like to tell CNH that since you are manufacturing tractors in Uttar Pradesh, you can also manufacture bulldozers here. There will automatically be demand for them in the country and abroad because it has already become a brand here,  Adityanath said.Read more: Five-year-old Kanpur girl gifts bulldozer toy to UP CM Yogi Adityanath, receives sweet advice in return; viral video shows interactionThe chief minister was virtually addressing the groundbreaking ceremony of CNH Industrial's tractor manufacturing plant in Sector 8D of the Yamuna Expressway Industrial Development Authority (YEIDA) area.Making a pitch for the state's improved law and order situation, Adityanath said UP, which faced several questions over 'neglect, backwardness and lawlessness' before 2017, had transformed from a 'state of unrest' into one of celebration under the guidance of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Uttar Pradesh has moved from the rule of mafia to the rule of law,  he said.He attributed the improvement in law and order not just to police recruitment and modernisation but also to the government's zero-tolerance policy towards crime and criminals.Read more: Bulldozers will act against anyone encroaching on monuments, govt land: AdityanathAdityanath noted that a strong law and order environment had helped UP move rapidly towards becoming a destination for ease of doing business, fearless business and investor confidence.He mentioned that companies from India and abroad were now lining up to invest in the state, which had established a new identity as one of the country's major investment destinations.Adityanath also referred to the transformation of the Jewar region, saying the area, which was once notorious for crime and violence, was now emerging as a major investment destination.He credited farmers, public representatives and local people for contributing to the region's development, saying their cooperation had helped bring large investments to the area.The remarks came as the state government seeks to showcase its law and order record and investment-friendly environment ahead of the 2027 UP Assembly elections.

matches.company: Honda Motor Company, Ltd. Common Stock
matches.title: Honda to invest $3 billion in Ohio plant to make hybrid vehicles, create 2,000 jobs
matches.full_text: Washington: Japanese automaker Honda Motor will build a new $3 billion auto plant in Ohio to make hybrid vehicles, creating 2,000 jobs, it said on Monday.The company said the plant will be able to produce 240,000 vehicles annually and begin production in 2029. It will increase its US auto production capacity to 1.3 million vehicles annually, and North American capacity to 1.9 million.Also Read: Mercedes plans bigger India play with greater localisation of partsHonda is also making a C$867 million ($613.6 million) commitment to its Canadian operations, including a C$166 million investment in its Alliston, Ontario, operations, maintaining its 4,000-strong Canadian workforce.The Canadian government said it is investing C$313 million in the Alliston project.Honda plans another $338 million investment in Ohio, and unspecified new investments in Georgia and Alabama.Also Read: Indiaâs luxury car buyers are paying a premium for exclusivity, says JLR India MDThe company announced plans in May to add 15 new Honda and Acura hybrid models worldwide by 2030. It also announced it would scrap electric vehicle sales goals and indefinitely suspended an $11 billion Canada EV project as part of a $9 billion EV writedown.Honda said it will invest in Alabama to build a new V6 hybrid engine and retool its Ohio engine plant to build a new four-cylinder engine. It will also retool transmission plants in Ohio and Georgia, and plans to reintroduce engine production in Ontario.A number of foreign automakers have announced major new investments as they face tariffs imposed by President Donald Trump's administration.Last month, Volkswagen luxury unit Audi said it would build a $4 billion assembly plant near Macon, Georgia to open in the early 2030s that would produce 200,000 SUVs annually and employ 4,500 workers.Reuters reported last month that Trump's administration had promised tariff relief to Audi to help secure the plant's future. US officials told Audi executives the government plans to offer broad relief from tariffs for automakers making significant investments in US production.

matches.title: Tata Motors-Iveco will focus on building a global CV business: N Chandrasekaran
matches.full_text: Mumbai: Tata Motors and Iveco Group are aiming to build a global commercial vehicle business focused on growth rather than consolidation, N Chandrasekaran, chairman, Tata Sons, said on Tuesday, outlining the rationale behind the transatlantic deal.The $4.32 billion acquisition of the Italian truck and bus maker marked the biggest overseas deal for Tata Motors in the CV segment and the largest by a Tata Group automotive entity since the 2008 acquisition of Jaguar Land Rover from Ford Motor Company for $2.3 billion.  This should not be seen as a consolidation effort,  said Chandrasekaran, also the chairman of Tata Motors and Iveco Group, at a press conference in Turin.  This is about the future. Also read: Indian auto's real test lies ahead after firecracker start to festive season135512105Announced July 30, 2025, the Iveco deal got completed on October 30, 2026, with Tata Motors announcing settlement of its tender offer, securing an 89.42% stake in the CV maker and making it an indirect unit. Remaining steps towards acquiring the balance stake and delisting Iveco are underway.The combined entity will have annual revenues of about $24 billion and sales volume of nearly 600,000 vehicles, with a presence in more than 130 countries, over 73,000 employees and 9,300 sales and service touchpoints.Girish Wagh, managing director and chief executive of Tata Motors said the companies' complementary geographical presence offered significant opportunities. While Tata Motors brings leadership in India and a growing presence in Asia, the Middle East and Africa, Iveco has established operations across Europe and Latin America, he said.  The opportunity is not to make one organisation more like the other,  he said.  It is to bring out the best in both. Also read: Tata Projects wins contract to build global automaker's plant in MaharashtraChandrasekaran expects volumes and revenues in the combined enterprise to grow significantly in the coming five years, alongside an improvement in margins. He didn't provide specific targets, saying the management teams would outline the business plan.A key area of collaboration will be bringing Iveco vehicles to India and leveraging Tata Motors' platforms for international markets. Chandrasekaran said some Iveco products identified as relevant to India would initially be introduced through semi-knocked-down manufacturing and subsequently localised. It is not simply about greater scale or wider footprint,  said Wagh.  It is about the new possibilities that this footprint creates, giving us a significantly greater runway for growth across markets, products and technologies. He also pointed to opportunities in components and batteries, while Tata Motors' platforms could be taken to other markets through Iveco. On powertrains, Chandrasekaran said Iveco's FPT engine business could expand into industrial applications across India, Africa and Asia, leveraging Tata Motors' distribution network. matches.company: Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corp
matches.title: Ashwini Vaishnaw launches Semicon 2.0 portal, says 50% of units approved under ECMS are SMES, MSMEs
matches.full_text: Union Electronics and Information Technology Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw on Friday launched the Semicon 2.0 Web Application Portal and announced that 50 per cent of the units approved under the Electronics Components Manufacturing Scheme (ECMS) belong to small and medium enterprises (SMEs) or micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs).Speaking at the launch event, Vaishnaw said the government would begin accepting applications under pillars two, three and four of the semiconductor programme, marking another step towards strengthening India's electronics and semiconductor manufacturing ecosystem. A lot of design expertise is getting building up lots of new things are coming...lots of new things are coming, and today onwards we'll start receiving the applications for the pillar two, three, and four,  he said, adding that  50 per cent of the units approved are SMEs or MSMEs. Vaishnaw emphasised that India's electronics manufacturing journey has gradually progressed from assembling finished products to manufacturing modules, components and raw materials, helping deepen domestic capabilities across the value chain.Recalling the initial phase of India's mobile phone manufacturing journey, he said,  When we started the mobile phone journey. journey, people used to laugh at us. People used to think that because we have an assembly, or screwdriver technology, all kinds of things. Explaining the government's approach, Vaishnaw said the objective was to systematically move towards higher levels of manufacturing integration rather than remain dependent on assembling finished products. The journey was to go step by step from finished product to the modules, to the components, to the materials,  he said.The Minister also highlighted India's growing capabilities in manufacturing critical electronics components and materials, including battery cells, copper foils and copper-clad laminates used in printed circuit boards (PCBs) Today we are making the entire battery cell. We are making copper foils. We are making copper-clad laminates for PCBs. In a sense, throughout that value chain, we are going deep with each program, with each approval,  he added.

matches.company: ASA  Gold and Precious Metals Limited
matches.title: Dhanteras expected to generate over Rs 1 lakh crore in business across India: CAIT
matches.full_text: The Dhanteras festival is expected to generate business worth more than Rs 1 lakh crore across the country on Friday, with gold and silver sales alone estimated to contribute over Rs 60,000 crore, according to the Confederation of All India Traders (CAIT).The trade body noted that festive buying enthusiasm remains strong, with consumers continuing to purchase jewellery, silver coins and traditional gifts during the festival.According to the All India Jewellers and Goldsmith Federation (AIJGF), demand for lightweight jewellery, silver coins and traditional gift items has increased in the market, indicating that high prices have not dampened consumer interest in festive purchases.ALSO READ | Dhanteras 2026: A 12% demand surge awaits Indian gold market even as prices hit two-week highThe federation shared that the jewellers are witnessing demand for lightweight gold jewellery in 14-carat and 18-carat categories, as consumers look for options amid elevated gold prices.Apart from gold jewellery, silver coins and decorative items are also attracting buyers. Traditional auspicious decorative articles and figurines of fish, tortoise and elephants are among the products witnessing increased demand in the market, the federation said.ALSO READ | 'Goldâs rally is not just about wars, itâs fundamentally linked to $40 tn US debt': WGC India CEO Sachin JainDhanteras is considered an important occasion for purchasing gold, silver and other goods, with many consumers making purchases as part of their festive traditions.This year, however, high precious metal prices have influenced buying preferences, with demand shifting towards lightweight jewellery and other relatively smaller purchases.Gold prices have moderated marginally during the past week, but as compared to last year, the prices have surged by around 20 per cent. Gold is trading at Rs 1,41,840/10 gram for 24 karat at the time of reporting.The expected business of more than Rs 1 lakh crore includes trading activity across the country during the festival, while gold and silver are estimated to account for more than Rs 60,000 crore of the total business, CAIT said.The All India Jewellers and Goldsmith Federation said it would issue a detailed press release by the evening after assessing sales trends and consumer response across markets nationwide.The final assessment is expected to provide a clearer picture of actual sales during the day, including the performance of gold and silver jewellery, coins and other festive products.

matches.title: Rs 37,500 cr coal gasification push: CDEP-CWS study identifies priority chemicals to cut import
matches.full_text: New Delhi: Hydrogen, synthetic natural gas (SNG), methanol and ammonia should be prioritised for production from coal to reduce India's dependence on imported fuels, fertilisers and industrial chemicals, according to a new study.The study by Centre for Domestic Economy Policy Research (C-DEP) and the Centre for WTO Studies (CWS) ranks 23 coal-derived products across eight economic, industrial and strategic parameters to guide investments under the government's Rs 37,500-crore scheme for promoting surface coal and lignite gasification projects.Also Read: Global oil market to return to surplus in Q4 2026, larger supply build expected in 2027: IEAHydrogen emerged as the highest-priority product, followed by SNG, methanol, ammonia, dimethyl ether (DME), LNG, LPG, urea and diammonium phosphate (DAP), the study said.The recommendations come as India seeks to expand coal gasification capacity to reduce its reliance on imported energy and fertiliser products.Also Read: Indiaâs fuel demand to keep climbing until 2034 despite EV boomThe government scheme aims to facilitate the gasification of an additional 75 million tonne of coal and lignite annually, while the country's target is to achieve 100 million tonne of coal gasification capacity by 2030.India imported nearly USD 37 billion worth of LPG, LNG, urea and DAP in 2024, underscoring the potential for domestic coal-based production to substitute imports. LPG and LNG imports alone exceeded USD 27 billion, while urea and DAP imports accounted for another USD 9.6 billion, the report said.The study, titled  Coal-to-Chemicals Policy in India: A Strategic Framework for Product Prioritisation under the National Coal Gasification Mission , argues that investments should be directed towards products offering the greatest potential for import substitution, economic returns and strategic supply security.Addressing the report's release, Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board (PNGRB) Chairperson Anil Kumar Jain said coal gasification in India was still at an early stage and that the commercial viability of technologies suited to Indian coal needed to be established, according to a statement issued by the organisers. While import dependence, supply security and strategic importance should guide product prioritisation, we must first allow industry to test these technologies and establish their feasibility. The government has created the necessary policy and financial support. The next step is for industry to demonstrate commercially viable projects, after which a more targeted product prioritisation framework can be developed,  he said.C-DEP President Jaijit Bhattacharya said the government's Rs 37,500-crore commitment made it important to identify products that could deliver the greatest economic benefits. matches.company: Clean Energy Technologies, Inc. - Common Stock
matches.title: India seeks to triple clean energy capacity to 900 gigawatts by 2035, but major hurdles remain
matches.full_text: Bengaluru: With the United Nations climate talks underway, India has set an ambitious goal of installing enough clean power to supply more than 1 billion homes by 2035, and has approved nearly $20 billion in power grid upgrades to ease bottlenecks that prevent some solar and wind energy from reaching consumers.The world's most populous country and one of the biggest carbon polluters is also among the fastest to expand clean power. Accelerating the shift away from fossil fuels is a key goal of this year's climate talks, known as COP31, in Turkey.India announced the 900-gigawatt goal in late September. It covers non-fossil power sources, including solar, wind, hydropower and nuclear energy. It is nearly twice India's existing target of 500 gigawatts of clean power by 2030. India's current clean power capacity of just over 300 gigawatts ranks it third behind China and the United States.Experts say meeting the target could lower electricity costs, curb coal construction and accelerate the transition to clean energy.The push comes as India struggles to use all the renewable electricity it can generate because of inadequate transmission infrastructure. The new goal refers to installed generating capacity, rather than the amount of electricity actually produced. If the grid doesn't catch up, then there is no way India can meet this target,  Nikit Abhyankar from the India Energy and Climate Centre at the University of California, Berkeley, said.  A robust and innovative transmission grid is an absolute must. The government also approved nearly $20 billion in funding for transmission infrastructure and battery storage under its Green Energy Corridor plan.Cheaper clean electricity could reduce India's reliance on coalEconomist Ajay Shah of the Mumbai-based XKDR Forum described the transition as the emergence of an Indian  electrostate,  in which electricity increasingly replaces coal and petroleum products. So now in India you have two assets - not only do you have cheap labour, you also have cheap energy,  Shah said.The shift mirrors a global trend toward cleaner power, even as fossil fuel energy remains a key energy source amid rising electricity demand. Brazil, which ranks close behind India in clean energy capacity, projects renewables will supply nearly 90% of its electricity in the next decade, even as it expands oil and gas production. In the United States, where President Donald Trump supports fossil fuels, electricity demand is expected to grow by 40%, with natural gas remaining a major source.India's clean energy expansion could help industries replace costly imported fossil fuels with domestically produced electricity. Abhyankar said solar and wind power, even when combined with battery storage, are increasingly cost-competitive with power from coal, oil and natural gas.Lower generation costs could eventually translate into cheaper electricity for households, though utilities also factor in transmission costs and other expenses.There are concern

matches.title: Pichai tops global Indian leaders’ list as Alphabet hits $4.2 trillion
matches.full_text: Bengaluru Sundar Pichai, CEO of Alphabet, has topped the HSBC Hurun Global Indians List 2026, with the company’s valuation reaching $4.2 trillion. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella ranked second, with Microsoft valued at $2.6 trillion, followed by Sanjay Mehrotra of Micron Technology at $1.4 trillion. The list recognises people of Indian origin, irrespective of nationality, who have founded or lead some of the world’s most valuable companies headquartered outside India. Alphabet’s valuation surged 98%, overtaking Microsoft, whose value declined 17%. Collectively, companies led by global Indians are now worth $15 trillion, up 53% since 2024. The top five account for $9.1 trillion, or 61% of the total, while the top 10 represent nearly 70%, at $10.5 trillion. Google extends voluntary buyout offers to employees in several countries Google extends voluntary buyout offers to employees in several countries Alphabet’s workforce has grown steadily in recent quarters, but it has sought to shift resources toward priority areas Google extends voluntary buyout offers to employees in several countries storyline 1 These companies employ 5.3 million people and generate annual revenues of $2.5 trillion. The 2026 edition features 236 individuals leading 200 companies, with 89 newcomers. Among the prominent entrants are Shailesh Jejurikar of Procter & Gamble, ranked sixth, and Kunal Shah of WhatsApp, ranked 14th. The entry threshold more than doubled to $2.5 billion from $1.2 billion. Africa makes its debut through Arvind Pathak, Group Managing Director of Dangote Group, extending the list’s geographical reach to five continents. Professionals constitute 53% of the entrants, while first-generation entrepreneurs account for 44%. The remaining 3% are second-generation leaders. Mercor co-founders Adarsh Hiremath and Surya Midha, both 23, are the youngest entrants. Romesh Wadhwani of SymphonyAI, 79, is the oldest. The average age is 55. Indian institutions continue to play a significant role in shaping global leadership. As many as 58% of entrants completed their undergraduate education in India. matches.company: Air Products and Chemicals, Inc. Common Stock
matches.title: INOX Air Products plans 27% capacity expansion on buoyant demand
matches.full_text: Mumbai INOX Air Products plans to add 5,235 tonnes per day (TPD) of industrial gas capacity by March 2027 through 12 new locations, as it seeks to capitalise on rising demand from India’s steel, solar and semiconductor industries. https:\/\/www.thehindubusinessline.com\/stocks\/inox-air-products-ltd\/ The expansion will increase its on-site capacity by 27 per cent to 20,388 TPD from 16,074 TPD as of March, 2026, while merchant liquid gas capacity will rise 18 per cent to 6,027 TPD from 5,106 TPD, according to its Draft Red Herring Prospectus filed with SEBI. Of the proposed addition, 4,314 TPD will be in the on-site segment and 921 TPD in merchant liquid gases. The company expects to increase its operating locations from 57 to 69, with six new facilities in West and Central India, three in the South, two in the North and one in the East. Steel will account for nearly 84 per cent of the upcoming on-site capacity, followed by solar at 7 per cent, non-ferrous metals at 5.5 per cent and electronics and semiconductors at 2.5 per cent. Steel contributed 41 per cent of the company’s revenue in FY26, against 37 per cent in the previous fiscal. The company has secured a contract worth about $150 million from Tata Steel for two Air Separation Units at Meramandali in Odisha. It has 10 on-site contracts under execution, in addition to 41 commissioned contracts. INOX Air Products is also expanding its speciality gases business to tap opportunities in India’s semiconductor and solar manufacturing sectors. It has commissioned ultra-high-purity gas plants at Hosur and Manali and is developing a speciality gas hub at Dholera, Gujarat, involving an initial investment of around ₹500 crore. According to the CRISIL report, India’s industrial gases market is expected to grow at 9–12 per cent annually between FY26 and FY32. The proposed IPO comprises an offer for sale of up to 7.72 crore shares by existing shareholders. The company will not receive any proceeds from the issue.

matches.company: Cathay Group Holdings Inc
matches.title: Cathay Group expands, upgrades fleet
matches.full_text: The Cathay Group has announced that it has ordered 14 more regional widebody and narrowbody aircraft as it continues to expand and upgrade its fleet to support its long-term growth plans. Cathay has exercised purchase rights for 11 more Airbus A330-900 aircraft, on top of the 30 it ordered in 2024. Additionally, Cathay has exercised purchase rights for three more Airbus A321neo narrowbody aircraft, on top of the 32 Airbus A321neo and A320neo aircraft it ordered in 2023. The A330-900 will support the growth of the Hong Kong-based airline’s regional network and enhance passenger and cargo capacity, while the A321neo will build on low-cost subsidiary HK Express’ growth potential, with a focus on destinations in the Chinese mainland and other short-haul routes, according to a company statement. E-mobility in Vietnam’s waterways CMA CGM, Nike and Gemadept have jointly launched an electric inland waterway transport solution in Vietnam, designed to support Nike’s supply chain decarbonisation efforts. The 100 per cent electric barge will connect Nike’s inland drop-off location in Ho Chi Minh City (formerly Binh Duong province) to Gemalink deep-sea terminal, covering a 180-km round trip with zero direct greenhouse gas emissions. Powered by batteries and certified renewable electricity from a dedicated solar farm at Gemalink, the solution is expected to avoid approximately 778 tonnes of carbon dioxide emissions annually. The end-to-end solution brings together an electric barge, dedicated charging infrastructure and renewable energy to accelerate lower-carbon logistics, a media release said.

matches.company: CRITICAL MINERALS GROUP LIMITED
matches.title: LICO Materials targets ₹450-500 crore revenue in current fiscal: CEO
matches.full_text: Lithium-ion battery recycling and refurbishing firm LICO Materials is targeting revenue of about â¹450-500 crore in 202627, driven by higher material-processing volumes, improved capacity utilisation, and greater availability of end-of-life lithium-ion batteries, its CEO Gaurav Dolwani said.The company recorded revenue of approximately â¹350 crore in 202526, Dolwani said, adding that its processing capacity has expanded significantly since the company last discussed its operations around March last year.The development assumes significance in the wake of the country's fast-expanding electric vehicle market and a growing push to build a domestic battery-recycling ecosystem that can recover critical minerals and bring down dependence on imports."For FY202627, we are targeting revenue of around â¹450-500 crore," Dolwani, who is also the founder of the company, told PTI in an interview, adding that the growth will be driven by higher material-processing volumes and improved capacity utilisation.More batteries are becoming available in the market as electric two- and three-wheeler adoption grows. The company has also been able to import batteries from other parts of the world, despite the challenges involved, which has helped it access material more successfully than some of its peers."Our current battery-processing capacity is around 4 GWh (gigawatt-hour). We aim to increase it to approximately 10 GWh over the next three years. We expect domestic cell manufacturing to expand over the same period, which should support the development of the battery ecosystem," he explained.He further said that cell manufacturing has taken longer than initially anticipated and involves significant technological challenges. Some companies have established pilot lines, invested in R&D, and learned from earlier challenges."Developing cells is extremely difficult, and we should recognise the complexity of the task and give the industry time to develop. The policy intent is right, but execution remains the key challenge," he said.When asked if the company is looking to expand geographically, Dolwani said that LICO Materials is working with job-work partners in Uttar Pradesh and Haryana and would like to strengthen its presence in this region. The company is also looking at western India, including Gujarat. Over time, the company may establish its own facility or acquire an existing business with relevant capabilities.Founded in 2021, LICO Materials works to recover, reprocess, and reintegrate battery materials into the battery value chain.The company operates in battery recycling and repurposing through its facility in Bengaluru, Karnataka. It processes end-of-life lithium-ion batteries, recovers materials used in battery manufacturing, and gives usable cells a second life through LiGRID, its battery energy storage system.

matches.title: Aayush Wellness enters shilajit segment with launch of Himalayan drops
matches.full_text: Aayush Wellness Ltd has entered the shilajit-based wellness supplement segment with the launch of Himalayan Shilajit Drops, seeking to diversify its nutraceutical portfolio and tap growing demand for products targeting energy, stamina and vitality.The launch comes amid projected growth in the global shilajit market, which was valued at $206.64 million in 2025 and is expected to reach $436.72 million by 2034, expanding at a compound annual growth rate of 8.67 per cent during 2026-34, the company said in a statement.Asia-Pacific accounted for around 61 per cent of the global market in 2025, while liquid shilajit products made up 60.72 per cent, indicating the growing relevance of the region and liquid formulations, it said.Aayush Wellness said its new product contains Himalayan-sourced shilajit extract in liquid-drop form and is positioned to support daily energy, stamina and vitality. The formulation is described as rich in fulvic acid and minerals, with heavy-metal testing.The product will add to the company's nutraceutical portfolio, which includes offerings across sleep, immunity, gut health, liver care, respiratory wellness and metabolic health.The company is also looking at opportunities beyond India, particularly in Southeast Asia, where it sees potential demand for natural-origin wellness products and traditional herbal ingredients.Aayush Wellness has established a wholly owned subsidiary in Singapore, which it said could provide a base to explore international business opportunities and wider regional markets. Any overseas launch of the shilajit drops would be subject to applicable regulatory and market-entry requirements."With the launch of Himalayan Shilajit Drops, we are further diversifying our nutraceutical portfolio and expanding our presence across emerging wellness categories," said Naveena Kumar, Managing Director of Aayush Wellness."Our broader objective is to build a diversified consumer wellness business with opportunities across India and international markets," she said.The company cited estimates from the Ministry of Food Processing Industries that India's nutraceutical market was valued at $30.37 billion in 2024 and is projected to grow at a CAGR of 13.6 per cent between 2025 and 2030.Aayush Wellness, listed on the BSE, said the launch was part of its strategy to expand its consumer wellness business through product diversification and exploration of domestic and overseas markets.Increasing lifestyle demands, changing dietary habits and growing awareness of preventive healthcare are driving consumer interest in products focused on everyday energy, stamina and overall wellness. matches.company: Hyperscale Data, Inc. Common Stock
matches.title: Black Box Q2 profit rises 30.6% to ₹72.6 crore; revenue up 22.2%
matches.full_text: Essar Group's IT firm Black Box on Friday reported a 30.6 per cent increase in consolidated net profit to Rs 72.68 crore for the July-September quarter of FY27, aided by growth in data centre and enterprise businesses.The Mumbai-headquartered company had posted a net profit of Rs 55.65 crore in the year-ago period, according to a regulatory filing by the company.Black Box's revenue from operations rose 22.2 per cent to Rs 1,936.30 crore, up from Rs 1,584.59 crore in Q2 FY26.Sequentially, the profit and revenue rose 30 per cent and 13 per cent, respectively.Growth was driven by execution across hyperscale data centre infrastructure and enterprise solutions, supported by growing momentum in its technology products business, the company said in a statement.Black Box secured over USD 250 million in data centre orders in the first half of FY27. A substantial pipeline of large hyperscale deals is expected to drive significant order wins and accelerate growth in the coming quarters, it said.The company's order backlog reached USD 1,044 million at the end of the September quarter, up 88 per cent year-on-year. It secured new orders worth USD 298 million during the quarter, up 37 per cent."These results reinforce our confidence in scaling the business towards our immediate growth goal of USD 2 billion in revenue. Our data centre business is a powerful growth engine, with significant orders from multiple hyperscalers and repeat wins expanding our role in their infrastructure investments," Black Box whole-time director and CEO Sanjeev Verma said."Our strong US presence, deep expertise and proven execution position us to capture a greater share of accelerating data centre investment, supported by a substantial opportunity pipeline," Verma said, adding that growing enterprise and technology products businesses across the US and international markets further strengthen the growth outlook.The company said it is confident of achieving FY27 guidance of 23-27 per cent revenue growth and 38-50 per cent growth in profit after tax, "with profit growth expected to remain in high double digits for the next few years along with stronger cash flow generation". It expects to exit the year with an order backlog of USD 1.3-1.4 billion.The company is progressing with its plan to recruit nearly 3,000 professionals by FY30, primarily in the US, with hiring underway for major data centre projects.
